messages.subject: [Picante-devel] New developer and manuscript plans
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Helene Morlon, a postdoc at the University of Oregon, is joining the  
picante developers and will be adding some functions to calculate  
measures of phylogenetic beta diversity. Welcome Helene!

I have received several requests from picante users who want a way to  
cite the package. I would like to begin preparing a manuscript  
describing the picante package for publication as an application note  
in a bioinformatics journal. We should look into publication funding  
options since I think it would be good to publish in an open-access  
journal. My suggestion is that everyone who has contributed code to  
the package should be included as an author on the manuscript, but  
that the developers will be first authors in order of the magnitude of  
their contributions to the package and/or manuscript, and that we will  
note this in the manuscript. Does this sound fair? I'll get in touch  
with developers individually in the near future to discuss further.

Best,
Steve

I think that is a great idea and it sounds fair. I am happy to 
contribute manuscript text and images on all the code I have written.

Now for some rambling open ended questions that maybe we can think about:

Do we want to start with an outline being passed around? Do you have a 
target journal in mind? Is it the same journal that Steve wrote his 
phylocom article? Would NESCent perhaps pay for open access since Peter 
and I were funded through them/Google this summer... perhaps Hilmar 
would know? Would we include examples of all the functions or just 
highlight some functions?

No answers needed now, but we should keep the Qs in mind as we go about 
this.

Matt

PS Nice work on your PNAS paper Helene!

messages.subject: [Picante-devel] New developer and manuscript plans
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

> Do we want to start with an outline being passed around?

Sounds like a good idea. I will draw up an outline and circulate.

> Do you have a target journal in mind? Is it the same journal that  
> Steve wrote his phylocom article? Would NESCent perhaps pay for open  
> access since Peter and I were funded through them/Google this  
> summer... perhaps Hilmar would know? Would we include examples of  
> all the functions or just highlight some functions?

I was thinking Bioinformatics would be a good target journal but I'm  
open to suggestions. There are open-access journals such as BMC  
Bioinformatics that would be suitable as well. I am not sure if  
NESCent has support for open access publication costs. Bioinformatics  
has no page charges but does have a pay-to-publish option to make the  
article open access IIRC. We published a Phylocom application note  
there, here is the link to get an idea of the format:
http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btn358

The length limit for application notes is quite short so I think the  
best approach is not to give a general overview of the kinds of  
analyses the package can do, maybe highlight one or two functions.

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject: [Picante-devel] New developer and manuscript plans
messages.body_plain:
Hi all - sorry for the silence on my part. First off, congrats and  
welcome to your new developer!

On Nov 14, 2008, at 1:40 PM, Steven Kembel wrote:

> I was thinking Bioinformatics would be a good target journal but I'm
> open to suggestions.

Yes that would be a good target.

> There are open-access journals such as BMC Bioinformatics that would  
> be suitable as well.

There is also Evolutionary Bioinformatics:

http://www.la-press.com/evolutionary-bioinformatics-journal-j17

This is where we published the Phyloinformatics Hackathon report:

http://www.la-press.com/the-2006-nescent-phyloinformatics-hackathon-a-field-report-a480

If you want to reach mostly ecologists, there is also Molecular  
Ecology Resources (f.k.a. Molecular Ecology Notes):

http://www.blackwellpublishing.com/journal.asp?ref=1755-098X&site=1

GeoPhylobuilder was published there. However, the journal apparently  
requires the transfer of copyright, which is not at all required for a  
commercial publisher (as OUP demonstrates, for example), and IMHO  
should not be rewarded. But I'm not the author or co-author and so  
should have no say in this :-)

> I am not sure if NESCent has support for open access publication  
> costs.


There is no general policy that NESCent would sponsor or subsidize  
open access publication costs from our sponsored projects. However,  
you would be welcome to use Google's Summer of Code organization  
payment share from your project ($500) for this purpose (I believe you  
or Matt haven't used that yet for meeting face-to-face, and don't seem  
to have urgent plans to do so?). If that would not suffice to help  
cover the costs, let me know.

	-hilmar
--

: Hilmar Lapp  -:-  Durham, NC  -:- hlapp at duke dot edu :
===========================================================
